summary: Gu Rong Gyalsé Chökyi Lodrö studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Shechen Gyaltsab.

Gualtherus Hendrik Mees was a religious studies and Indology scholar. He earned an M.A. from the University of Cambridge (~1925–1928), studied under Jean Philippe Vogel, and completed an LL.D. at Leiden University (~1928–1935).

Guang Xing is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at SOAS, University of London under Tadeusz Skorupski and Timothy Hugh Barrett. He became an assistant professor at the University of Hong Kong (~2003) and visited UBC in 2007.

Guangchang Fang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He served as a researcher at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1986–2000) and became a professor at Shanghai Normal University (~2000).
Guankong was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He taught at the Institute of Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Studies and served as a professor at the Buddhist Academy of China in 1957.

Gudo Wafu Nishijima was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied law at the University of Tokyo and trained under Kodo Sawaki and Rempo Niwa. He lectured at the University of Tokyo and the Eastern Institute, and founded Dogen Sangha International.

Gudrun Bühnemann is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies scholar. She studied at Bonn, Münster, and Vienna (under Ernst Steinkellner), held research posts in India and Japan, and became a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1992.

Gudrun Melzer is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned her PhD at the University of Munich under Jens-Uwe Hartmann. As of 2026, she holds research posts at Munich, Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and IIBS.

Guilherme de Vasconcelos Abreu was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Coimbra, with Martin Haug, and Abel Bergaigne. He founded the Associação Promotora dos Estudos Orientais e Glóticos and became Professor of Sanskrit at Curso Superior de Letras.

Guillaume Le Gentil studied at the Faculté de théologie catholique de Paris and the Collège de France. Specializing in history, archaeology, and other fields, he held a post at the Paris Observatory from ~1748 to 1792.

Guillaume Oisel is a linguist and Tibetologist who earned a doctorate in linguistics from Sorbonne Nouvelle University (2006–2013). In 2019, he held a teaching post (Docente) at the National University of San Marcos.
Gunapala Dharmasiri is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who held academic posts at the University of Peradeniya, attested in 1991 and 2008.
Gunilla Gren-Eklund is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. She studied under Stig Wikander and Nils Simonsson, and held an academic post at Uppsala University from ~1978 to 2005.
Gunnar Jarring was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He completed his studies at Lund University (~1926–1933) and subsequently held a post there from ~1933 to 1940.

Guo Jun is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. Educated at Fuyan Buddhist Institute, Monash University, and the University of Sydney, he studied under Sheng Yen, Song Nian, and Qinyin, and served as abbot of Mahabodhi Monastery (attested 2013).
Guohui Shi is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Rissho University (~1997–2005) under Kenyu Mitomo, while also studying under Sheng Yen, Hoyo Watanabe, and several other teachers.
Gurii Stepanov was a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Kazan Theological Seminary and Kazan Theological Academy (1902–1906), where he was appointed Docent of Kalmuk in 1909.

Gurinder Singh Mann, a religious studies and Indology scholar, earned degrees from Baring Union Christian College, Kent, Harvard, and Columbia (PhD ~1993). He taught at Columbia (1988–1999) and held the Sikh Studies Chair at UCSB (1999–2015).

id: P:Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga
summary: Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga was a religious studies scholar who earned his doctorate in theology at Leiden University. He served as professor at the University of Amsterdam (1935–1944) and docent at Utrecht University (1944–1957).

Gustaaf Houtman is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at SOAS, University of London (-1990) under Richard Burghart, Hla Pe, and John Okell, later serving there as Senior Teaching Fellow (attested 2014).
